notes: §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR2 (old GR1, renumbered by Amendment 2): inspection, 'which includes the comparison cycle, the establishment of boundaries for the BEFORE or AFTER phrase, and the mechanism for tallying and/or replacing', 'begins at the leftmost character position of the data item referenced by identifier-1, regardless of its class, and proceeds from left to right to the rightmost character position as described in general rules 6 through 8'. InspectEmitter.Emit reads identifier-1 once as its character image whatever its class (a signed numeric item de-signed and re-signed on the store) and CobolInspect.RunCycle starts at position 0 and advances rightward, past each match or by one position, until the last character; at 85 the direction is fixed because VersionConformancePass.VisitInspectStatement refuses BACKWARD below 2023 (COBOL0845, probed), so Tally, Replace and Convert always pass backward = false. Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness: signed, sign-separate, numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and group identifier-1, and the standard's examples 1 to 4 (§1985:VI.6.18.5), all as the rule gives. PARTIAL in one arm: CobolInspect.Region establishes the BEFORE boundary of an operand that also has an AFTER phrase by searching from the AFTER-derived start (`text.IndexOf(before, start)`), not from the leftmost character position of identifier-1, the 2023 wording (§2023:14.9.22.4 GR9 'the first character position that is eligible to participate up to, but not including, the first occurrence encountered of literal-2'); §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR8 b measures BEFORE 'from its leftmost character position up to, but not including, the' 'first occurrence of literal-2 within the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1'. An operand with only BEFORE or only AFTER, and every statement without them, conforms. kb/Work PB5120 (open) owns this defect at the same site and names GR8 only; this row waits on it.

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993, page VI-96) renumbered this rule (old GR1) and its reference ('general rules 5 through 7' to 'general rules 6 through 8'); the requirement is the printed one. §1985:VI.6.18.4 GR2: inspection 'begins at the leftmost character position of the data item referenced by identifier-1, regardless of its class, and proceeds from left to right to the rightmost character position'. §2023:14.9.22.4 GR3 repeats those words and adds 'unless BACKWARD is specified, in which case, inspection ... begins at the rightmost character position of the data item referenced by identifier-1, regardless of its class, and proceeds from right to left to the leftmost character position'. The 1985 format has no BACKWARD (§1985:VI.6.18.2 prints identifier-1 directly after INSPECT); §2023:14.9.22.2 prints an optional 'BACKWARD' before identifier-1 in every format, so a right-to-left inspection, refused in 1985, is accepted and given a result: a case added (family ruling). An INSPECT without BACKWARD runs the same in both. 'to': GR3 states the whole rule; §2023:14.9.22.4 GR8 states the start and direction of the comparison cycle in its own words ('starting with the leftmost character position, or, if BACKWARD is specified, the rightmost character position'; 'continues until the rightmost character position of the data item referenced by identifier-1 has participated in a match'), and §2023:14.9.22.4 GR9 those of the BEFORE and AFTER boundaries ('first eligible to participate in matching at the leftmost character position, or, if BACKWARD is specified, at the rightmost character position of identifier-1'; 'up to, but not including, the first occurrence encountered of literal-2'), the two things this rule says inspection 'includes'.
